title: udev regression causes Librem 5 USB rules using ID_PATH to stop matching
body: #26886 may have caused a regression, but I am not sure. This issue is a reminder about the regression reported in the linked Debian bug.

symptoms_visible: On the affected Librem 5, the modem disappears during early boot when the initramfs runs something like udevadm settle.
Other users with the same device and rules do not see this when they do not need the touchscreen during early boot.
N1.label: N1 early-boot USB disappearance characterized

symptoms_visible: After updating the packages that install the Librem 5 udev rules, I can no longer reproduce the modem disappearance in the default installed state.
N2.label: N2 updated downstream rules avoid symptom

symptoms_visible: If I restore the original udev rules, the modem reliably disappears again.
Changing a matching USB rule from power/persist=0 to power/persist=1 appeared to keep the device available.
N3.label: N3 original rules reproduce issue

symptoms_visible: With the original rules that match the hub interfaces through ENV{ID_PATH}, the expected port attributes are not applied and the USB reset makes the modem disappear.
With the rewritten rules matching the same interfaces through ENV{DEVPATH}, the attributes are applied and the modem remains available.
N3_x.label: N3_x power-persist explanation rejected

symptoms_visible: The original rules still reproduce the modem disappearance on the newer udev behavior.
N4.label: N4 old and new udev behavior compared

symptoms_visible: The proposed build works with the original rules; the modem remains available.
N5.label: N5 proposed fix verified

symptoms_visible: With a build containing the compatibility fix and the original Librem 5 rules, the modem remains available through the initramfs udev settle operation.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix confirmed

question_patterns: What observable failure occurs, and at what point during boot?
What disappears or disconnects when this regression is triggered?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The modem disappears during early boot. It happens when something like udevadm settle runs in the initramfs.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Nothing disconnects during boot; only a harmless warning is printed by udevadm.

question_patterns: Can you provide the installed udev rules and say which rules are copied into the initramfs?
Please collect the rules under /usr/lib/udev/rules.d and /etc/udev/rules.d, including the initramfs set.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There is nothing in /etc/udev/rules.d. I provided the contents of /usr/lib/udev/rules.d. The initramfs normally contains the standard firmware, default, device-mapper, block, storage, seat, network and driver rules; copying all installed rules into it does not change the issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The initramfs contains a separate local rule that is not present on the installed system, and removing that rule prevents the disconnection.
The same rule set is present, but it was copied by a different initramfs hook.

edges.comment: Messages c2-c12 from the affected Debian/Mobian reporter are folded into the simulated user side. The initial udevadm paths were not useful, so the focused evidence is the early-boot symptom and the actual installed/initramfs rule sets.

question_patterns: What changed when the issue stopped reproducing?
Which package update changed the behavior, and what do you observe with its current rules?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After updating the packages that install the Librem 5 udev rules, I can no longer reproduce the issue in the default installed state. The newer package has a different rule set.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The rules did not change; only the systemd package changed, and the issue disappeared after downgrading systemd.

edges.comment: Messages c15 and c19-c20 from participant1. Installing the updated downstream packages is a persistent system change, so the destination uses S2.

question_patterns: Can you restore the original rule set and confirm whether the original failure returns?
Does the behavior follow the old versus new udev rules?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. If I roll back to the original rules, the modem disappearance reliably comes back. With the updated rules it is not triggered.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Rolling back the rules does not bring the issue back; the modem now works with both rule sets.
The old rules reproduce it only after a second reboot, while the new rules still avoid it.

question_patterns: Which individual rule edit initially appeared to affect the disconnection?
What was the first rule line you narrowed the behavior to?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At first, changing the matching USB rule from ATTR{power/persist}="0" to ATTR{power/persist}="1" appeared to fix it.

edges.comment: Messages c18-c21. The old rule package is restored for reproduction, a persistent change represented by S3. Participant1 and participant2 are folded into one affected user side.

solution.intent: Treat disabling USB power persistence as the cause of the disconnection and redirect the issue to the Librem 5 rule maintainers without changing systemd.
solution.concrete_example: The rule sets power/persist to zero, so suspended devices are being treated as disconnected; report that power-setting rule to the Librem 5 team.

edges.comment: Messages c22 and c25-c26. The maintainer's power/persist explanation was explicitly corrected by participant3 and confirmed inaccurate by participant2. The relevant difference is that two rules matching hub interfaces through ENV{ID_PATH} no longer apply, while their ENV{DEVPATH} replacements work.

question_patterns: Please run udevadm info for both affected USB interface sysfs paths using a known-working old userspace and paste the raw output.
Can you compare the property output for those two interfaces on the older working setup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the working v247 setup, udevadm info for both USB interface paths includes ID_PATH and ID_PATH_TAG. One result contains ID_PATH=platform-xhci-hcd.4.auto-usb-0:0:1.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The old working setup also omits ID_PATH and ID_PATH_TAG from both interfaces.

question_patterns: Run the same udevadm info commands on the affected newer setup and paste the properties.
What does the same property query print on the newer system?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On udev 253.5, the normal udevadm info output for those USB interfaces has DEVPATH and the USB properties, but no ID_PATH or ID_PATH_TAG.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The newer affected setup includes exactly the same ID_PATH and ID_PATH_TAG values as v247.
The newer output is from udev 252 rather than 253, but it still omits both properties.

question_patterns: Please run the requested builtin probe for both sysfs paths and paste its raw output.
Can the newer tool compute the path properties when the relevant builtin is invoked directly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On the newer system, the direct builtin test prints ID_PATH=platform-xhci-hcd.4.auto-usb-0:0:1.0 and the corresponding ID_PATH_TAG for the first interface, with matching path properties for the second.

question_patterns: Can you provide normal udevadm test output for the same interfaces from both the old working and new affected behavior?
Please compare the rule-processing logs for those devices on the two versions.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The v247 udevadm test output contains ID_PATH and ID_PATH_TAG. The newer normal test output does not contain them, even though the separate builtin probe can print them.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both normal test logs invoke the same rules and produce the same path properties.

question_patterns: Please check the requested USB class sysfs files for the interface paths and report the exact result.
Do those interface directories contain the queried class attribute?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Those files do not exist under the interface paths; cat returns 'No such file or directory'. The parent USB device directories have bDeviceClass=09.

edges.comment: Messages c27-c53. Outputs come from participant2 and participant3, folded into one user side. The confused participant2 run labeled as old still used tool version 253 and is not treated as the old comparison; participant3 supplied the valid v247 output. The maintainer first attributed the old match to 71-seat, then explicitly withdrew that story after comparing normal test logs.

question_patterns: Could you test the proposed build with the original reproducing rule set and tell me what you observe?
Please retest using the provided candidate and the rules that previously made the modem disappear.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm it works. With the proposed build, the original reproducing setup no longer makes the modem disappear. Thanks!

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The proposed build still loses the modem with the original rules.

edges.comment: Messages c55-c57. This is pre-landing verification of a candidate change, so it is modeled as a measurement clarification. Participant2 performed the test and confirmed the result on an affected system.

solution.intent: Preserve ID_PATH compatibility for USB interfaces by arranging for their path properties to be imported again, so existing rules matching ENV{ID_PATH} continue to apply.
solution.concrete_example: Use the tested systemd change that restores path properties for USB interfaces. The earlier cleanup stopped an unrelated broad rule from incidentally invoking the path-property builtin for these interfaces; restoring an intentional import lets the existing Librem 5 ENV{ID_PATH} rules set the required port quirks again.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied raw old/new udevadm outputs: the old normal rule run produced ID_PATH for USB interfaces, the new normal run did not, and the newer builtin could still compute it directly. The maintainer inferred that the earlier broad 60-drm rule had incidentally invoked the path-property builtin for most USB interfaces and that the cleanup removed this side effect. The earlier 71-seat explanation was explicitly withdrawn and is not the accepted diagnosis.

edges.comment: Final diagnosis from c53-c55 and affected-user verification from c57. The technical resolution is to intentionally provide path properties for USB interfaces so existing downstream ENV{ID_PATH} rules remain functional. The thread establishes successful testing of the proposed change; release and merge logistics are not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: an earlier broad udev rule incidentally imported path properties for USB interfaces, and the cleanup removed that invocation, so existing ENV{ID_PATH}-based Librem 5 rules stopped matching.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the old/new udevadm evidence: the working old normal rule run supplies ID_PATH, the newer normal run omits it, and the newer direct builtin probe can still compute it.
Must recommend intentionally restoring path properties for USB interfaces, or an equivalent compatibility fix, so the original ID_PATH-based rules apply their required USB port attributes.
Must not settle on power/persist as the cause; that explanation was corrected in the thread, and the working DEVPATH rewrite demonstrates that the relevant failure is the unmatched interface rules.
Must not use the withdrawn 71-seat explanation as the root cause.
Must have an affected user verify a build containing the compatibility fix with the original reproducing rules before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: A systemd/udev maintainer opens the issue, while several technically capable Librem 5 and Mobian users supply rules, initramfs details, sysfs output, cross-version udev tests, and candidate-build verification; all affected participants are folded into one simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical and cooperative, with large verbatim command outputs. The user readily runs requested probes but may need exact commands and can confuse daemon, tool, or package versions; other affected participants correct those details with concrete evidence.
